subject: Insurance
title: The Mortality Table
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Mortality Table usable.

hook.text: Insurers know exactly how likely you are to die this year. A 25-year-old man has a 0.07% chance. At 65, it's 1.5%.

buildup.text: Mortality tables track death rates by age, gender, and health. They're built from millions of actual death records.

discovery.text: Premiums are priced from these tables. The higher your chance of dying, the more you pay. Math, not guesswork.

twist.text: Mortality has improved so much that life insurers keep profiting.

climax.text: The mortality table is life insurance's engine.

punchline.text: 0.07% at 25, 1.5% at 65. Your death probability sets your premium.

quiz.question: What do mortality tables measure?
options: Death rates by age and demographics
